etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Spanish cigarro, of uncertain origin; see that entry for more.

definitions.definition: A cylinder of tobacco rolled and wrapped with an outer covering of tobacco leaves, intended to be smoked.

quote.citation: 1907 August, Robert W[illiam] Chambers, chapter III, in The Younger Set, New York, N.Y.: D. Appleton & Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: Long after his cigar burnt bitter, he sat with eyes fixed on the blaze. When the flames at last began to flicker and subside, his lids fluttered, then drooped ; but he had lost all reckoning of time when he opened them again to find Miss Erroll in furs and ball-gown kneeling on the hearth […].

quote.citation: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 5, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:
quote.text: A waiter brought his aperitif, which was a small scotch and soda, and as he sipped it gratefully he sighed. ¶ ‘Civilized,’ he said to Mr. Campion. ‘Humanizing.’  […]  ‘Cigars and summer days and women in big hats with swansdown face-powder, that's what it reminds me of.’
